Detaille Island lies in Lallemand Fjord off the Loubet Coast. On its rocky shore stands the historic building of Base W, with high mountains and glaciers rising behind it. The base operated from 1956 to 1959.

The polar researchers worked on mapping, geology and meteorology. When the station was evacuated because of sea ice, many belongings were left behind, preserving the atmosphere of a small mid-20th-century research station. Today this historic site is cared for by the UK Antarctic Heritage Trust. Approaching and visiting the island depend on navigation conditions.

Off the coast of Floreana, the dark, jagged rocks of Devil's Crown rise from the ocean. They are the remains of a volcanic crater eroded by waves. From a boat, you can see the separate rocky outcrops and the water between them, making it easier to imagine how an earlier volcanic formation gradually became this seascape.

The main discoveries await beneath the surface. Fish, sea lions and turtles can be encountered around the rocks, while coral patches add color and detail to the underwater world. A few kicks of your fins are enough to transform a familiar ocean view into an entirely different environment. The wildlife varies from one outing to the next, so each sighting is a genuine discovery.

Devil's Crown is known for currents and swell, which makes it essential to assess the conditions and participants' readiness before entering the water. The guide chooses a suitable snorkeling area; viewing the rocks from a boat also reveals their shape and the seabirds that live around them. This is a memorable stop on a Galápagos journey for travelers interested in both volcanoes and ocean life.

Devil's Island, or Île du Diable, is part of the Îles du Salut archipelago in the Atlantic Ocean off Kourou. Along with Île Royale and Île Saint-Joseph, it is associated with the history of the French penal system. The name of the individual island is often used when referring to the entire archipelago, although these are distinct geographical entities.

The island's history includes the imprisonment of Alfred Dreyfus. Views of it from the sea and from neighboring Île Royale complement a visit to the surviving buildings of the archipelago's penal colony system. The Îles du Salut combine tropical island scenery with French Guiana's historic heritage, which here is closely connected with the coast and sea.

Diego de Alvear lies in the General López Department of Santa Fe Province. A stop here offers a glimpse of everyday rural life in Argentina, beyond its major cities and coastal resorts.

On a professional study trip, the Diego de Alvear area connects sections of the agricultural route between Pergamino and Venado Tuerto. The main focus of a visit is agricultural practice: no-till farming methods, machinery and farm organization. We arrange visits around the delegation's interests and allow time for questions to local specialists, making the journey useful for professional comparison.

A morning at Doka Estate begins among glossy coffee leaves and red cherries. Green slopes rise toward Poás Volcano, while the buildings of an old estate can be seen between the coffee plants. It is a pleasant place to slow down, walk alongside the bushes and discover coffee long before it reaches the cup.

Hacienda Doka is located in the Sabanilla area of Alajuela Province. During the tour, visitors see how coffee plants are grown, how the pulp is removed from the cherries, how the beans are processed and prepared for roasting. The historic production facilities reveal how much work goes into a familiar morning drink. At the end, you can explore different roasts and choose coffee to take home.

A visit to Doka fits naturally into a trip to Poás and the La Paz Waterfalls. On Ada Tours itineraries, this stop connects rural Costa Rica with volcanic landscapes and rainforest. The activities included, tastings and meals depend on the selected program; the season determines what work is taking place at the plantation when you visit.
